draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Athirappilly! The falls here are the largest in Kerala, dropping 81.5 feet on the Chalakudy River, which is why people call them the Niagara of South India.
draft.hungryLine: I don't know a named place to eat out here, so carry snacks. Chalakudy town is 24 km back down the road if you want more choice.

moodReplies.show-me-around: The falls viewpoint is a 5 min walk, and the Kannankuzhi Siva Temple is about 11 minutes on foot.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Find a quiet spot near the falls and take in the forest and little streams all around you.
moodReplies.surprise-me: This is the only place in the Western Ghats where four endangered hornbill species are seen.

legends.title: The Niagara of South India
legends.body: Ask anyone around here and they'll tell you these are Kerala's Niagara. The nickname stuck because no waterfall in the state is bigger.

legends.title: Home of four hornbills
legends.body: Environmentalists say this stretch of river is a one-of-its-kind riparian ecosystem in Kerala. It's the only place in the Western Ghats where four endangered hornbill species are seen.

tips.title: Look up for hornbills.
tips.body: Four endangered hornbill species live in the Athirappilly-Vazhachal forests, so keep your eyes on the treetops.

tips.title: Add Vazhachal Falls.
tips.body: It's just a short drive from Athirappilly, right by dense green forest.

story.title: A river from the Ghats
story.body: The Chalakudy River starts in the upper reaches of the Western Ghats. It tumbles over the falls here at the entrance to the Sholayar ranges, about 1000 feet above sea level.

story.title: A dam above the falls
story.body: The state proposed a hydroelectric dam on the Chalakudy River just above the waterfalls. A long fight over it began.

story.title: Still arguing
story.body: The controversy carried on through 2017. Environmentalists pointed out that the Western Ghats were already hurt by mining and hydroelectric projects.

story.title: Kerala's biggest falls
story.body: Athirappilly Falls is the largest waterfall in Kerala. The forests around it are full of endangered and endemic plants and animals.
